findings.title: WorkflowNavigator's three `'complete'` literals are `SliceStatus.status` values the design itself excludes from the sweep
findings.description: The site inventory (line 36), component table (line 75), and Migration Plan step 4 (line 90) all instruct sweeping "3 bare-string comparisons" in `WorkflowNavigator.ts` to `STATUS.Complete`. In the source those three literals are `WorkflowNavigator.ts:312` (`slice.status === 'complete'`), `:345` (`slice.status === 'complete'`), and `:588` (`return { ...base, status: 'complete', taskProgress }`) — all of type `SliceStatus['status']`, the lifecycle-position union. That is precisely the union that TD-3 (lines 104–106) and the Success Criteria (line 136, "SliceStatus.status remain untouched … not accidentally swept") say must be left alone, and the Verification Walkthrough's "After" tally (line 151) still counts these as remaining `SliceStatus.status` sites. WorkflowNavigator has no bare `NormalizedStatus` literals left — 241 already converted its three real `NormalizedStatus` comparisons to `STATUS.*` (`:319`, `:577`, `:695`). The design therefore gives contradictory instructions: following the sweep table/task 9 conflates the two status vocabularies TD-3 deliberately separates; following TD-3 means WorkflowNavigator contributes 0 sites and the "3 sites / 6 files / ~65 sites" inventory (and task 9) is wrong. Resolve before implementation — most cleanly by dropping WorkflowNavigator from the sweep and correcting the counts, or by explicitly revising TD-3 and line 136.

findings.title: The claim that "zero `.test.ts` files assert against these literals" is factually false
findings.description: The design states that "grep confirms zero `.test.ts` files assert against these literals," using this to justify excluding tests from scope and to justify relying on them as the regression guard. An actual grep of `packages/core` finds many, e.g. `tests/introspection/ArtifactIntrospector.test.ts:79` (`expect(result.data.status).toBe('in-progress')`), `ConsistencyChecker.test.ts:313/369/545/625` (`expect(...).toEqual({ key: 'status', value: 'in-progress' })`, `expect(...).toContain('not-started')`), and `ConsistencyChecker.reviewGate.test.ts:48` / `reviewGateWidened.test.ts:49` (`status: 'complete'`). The conclusion "no test changes are needed" still holds — swept values are byte-identical (`STATUS.X === 'x'`), tests live under `packages/core/tests` (outside the swept `src`), and retyping `inferredStatus` to the `NormalizedStatus` superset is backward-compatible — so scope is unaffected. But the stated premise is wrong; the design should correct it and state the real assumption explicitly (tests stay green because values are unchanged) rather than resting a scope decision on an incorrect "grep confirms" claim.
